chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Hisham narrated from you that you ordered him to perform the complete prayer (al-tamm) in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), and that was for the sake of the people.' He said, 'No, it was I and those who passed away from my fathers; when we entered Mecca, we completed the prayer and concealed ourselves from the people. And what we mentioned earlier regarding that it is appropriate to combine [the prayers] while staying for ten days is also based on recommendation (istihbab). And that which indicates this is what he narrated.'

key_terms.الاسْتِحْبَاب: Recommendation (a legal ruling less than obligatory but more than permissible)
key_terms.التِّمَام: Complete prayer (performing four rak'ahs as two in the two Sanctuaries)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining prayers and performing complete prayer in Mecca according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the historical context of the Ahl al-Bayt's practice of performing complete prayers in the two Sanctuaries to avoid public scrutiny during periods of political tension, and the general jurisprudential ruling for the community. He clarifies that while their specific action was driven by necessity and preference, the associated practice of combining prayers during the ten-day stay in Mecca remains a recommended act (istihbab) rather than a strict obligation, illustrating the nuanced application of *taqiyya* and practical wisdom in Shia fiqh.
